A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TETRIS research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original throughput, latency, token-acceptance, robustness, Medusa-integration, and batch-size experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds extra-draft-token sensitivity results for additional base draft lengths in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, greedy selection by cumulative acceptance probability, the draft-probability surrogate, and GPU implementation remain unchanged. The Medusa adaptation already appears in v1; v2 adds explanations rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ShareGPT, Arena, Tough, synthetic Sonnet prompts, and the Sonnet/Tough mixture. The added draft-length sensitivity experiment changes configurations within existing coverage, without introducing a new dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Standard SD, DSD, the no-SD reference, and baseline Medusa retain their corresponding comparisons. V2's expanded discussion of EAGLE-2 and newly cited MDSD does not introduce either as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.2 extends the extra-token sweep from base length k=4 to k=1, 2, and 3, varying 0–9 extra tokens across the existing three model settings. The main evaluation settings, metrics, hardware configurations, and 64-request load remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a focused sensitivity analysis testing whether the extra-token/VSR trend depends on choosing base length k=4 (Appendix C.2, Figure 7). Existing draft-quality mixing, Medusa, verification-success, and batch-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing three-trial summaries and mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged, including Figure 4, the latency plots, and Table 5. V2 introduces no changed run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: New Figure 7 reports additional VSR curves for base lengths k=1, 2, and 3, showing generally increasing VSR with extra tokens. Original numerical results and plotted curves are retained, including the 5.25% throughput and 6.13% latency improvements over the best baseline.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumption 1, Theorems 1–2, runtime lemma, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. New Appendix B.3 contextualizes the existing assumption without adding or revising formal results or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: batch-level draft selection, optimality under stated assumptions, and empirical throughput and latency benefits. Added future-work suggestions do not redefine the paper's core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix B.3 newly emphasize empirical usefulness when the global-optimality assumption is violated. Appendix C.2 explains the choice of k=4 and interprets the added sensitivity evidence. The sequential-pipeline limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly supplies a code repository URL. Section 5.3 specifies that end-to-end latency runs from client request submission to receipt of the final server response. These improve access and measurement documentation without establishing changes to the existing experiments.

R1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a focused comparison with EAGLE-2 and MDSD, while B.3 relates the existing assumption to prior analyses. V2 also adds Code Llama and data-selection references. These refine the established batch-versus-single-request positioning.

P1.justification: V2 adds localized explanations, appendix subsections B.2–B.3 and C.2, a broader-impacts appendix, acknowledgments, and correspondence information. It corrects wording such as VFS to VSR, while retaining most prose and the main section structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel Figure 7, enlarges and relocates Figure 1 and several plots, and reformats the pipeline diagram's legend. Existing figures are also relocated or renumbered; table structures and the overall visual format remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity experiment supports the extra-token finding beyond the original k=4 sweep. Code-access information, clearer latency documentation, and focused explanations of assumptions and prior work improve reproducibility and understanding. These are limited gains: the principal results and proofs remain unchanged, and the parallel-pipeline benefits still lack implementation-based validation.
